diagnosis_explanation: Your brain and spinal cord have a type of cancer. It is called central nervous system lymphoma. This means a kind of white blood cell grew in the wrong place. This can cause problems with how your brain and body work. We are treating this cancer. You also had germs in your blood. This is called bacteremia. Your blood count was also low. This is called pancytopenia. You also have high blood pressure. Your body also had trouble getting enough oxygen. This is called hypoxia. You have a rash near your anus. You also have diabetes. This means your body has trouble controlling sugar. You were given medicine to help prevent seizures. Your kidneys were also hurt during this time. This is called acute kidney injury.
medication_rationale:
High-Dose Methotrexate:
This medicine is a strong chemotherapy. It is used to treat cancer in your brain and spine. This medicine helps kill cancer cells. You may feel very tired or sick to your stomach. You might also get mouth sores. Call your doctor if you have a fever. Also call if you get chills or a rash.

Rituxan weekly:
This medicine helps your body fight cancer cells. It is a type of targeted therapy. It works by finding cancer cells. Then it tells your body to attack them. You may get flu-like symptoms. This can include fever or chills. You might also feel tired. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing. Also call if you get a rash.

Leucovorin 100 mg/m2 (for four doses):
This medicine helps protect your healthy cells. It is given with high-dose methotrexate. Methotrexate can harm healthy cells. Leucovorin lessens this harm. You should not notice any effects from this medicine. Call your doctor if you get a fever. Also call if you have any signs of infection.

Cefepime (for 14-day course):
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights infections caused by bacteria. Your body may have a bacterial infection. This medicine helps clear it up. You might get diarrhea. This is common. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Also call if you have severe stomach pain.

Vancomycin:
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights infections caused by bacteria. Your body may have a bacterial infection. This medicine helps clear it up. You might get red skin. This can happen if the medicine is given too fast. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Also call if you have severe stomach pain.

Cipro (changed):
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights infections caused by bacteria. Your body may have a bacterial infection. This medicine helps clear it up. You might get diarrhea. This is common. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Also call if you have severe stomach pain.

Aloe Vesta foam topically:
This foam is a skin protectant. It helps soothe your skin. It can also prevent irritation. You should apply it to the affected area. You will likely not notice any effects. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Also call if the skin becomes more red.

Silver gel topically:
This gel helps heal your skin. It can also prevent infection. It is used on your skin to help it heal. You should apply it to the affected area. You will likely not notice any effects. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Also call if the skin becomes more red.

Diflucan 200 mg daily (for 10-day course):
This medicine is an antifungal medicine. It treats fungal infections. You may be at risk for these infections. This medicine helps prevent them. You might get an upset stomach. This is common. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Also call if your skin turns yellow.

Sliding Scale Insulin as needed:
This medicine helps lower your blood sugar. Your blood sugar may be too high. This medicine is given based on your blood sugar reading. You might feel shaky or sweaty. This can happen if your blood sugar drops too low. Call your doctor if you have very low blood sugar.

Lantus insulin 35 units every night at bedtime:
This medicine lowers your blood sugar. It is a long-acting insulin. It helps keep your blood sugar steady. You might feel shaky or sweaty. This can happen if your blood sugar drops too low. Call your doctor if you have very low blood sugar.

Keppra twice daily:
This medicine helps control seizures. It is used if you have a history of seizures. It helps prevent them from happening. You may feel dizzy or tired. This is common. Call your doctor if you feel very sleepy. Also call if you get mood changes.

Lisinopril daily:
This medicine helps lower your blood pressure. It makes your heart work less hard. This helps protect your heart and kidneys. You might get a dry cough. This is common. Call your doctor if your face or lips swell. Also call if you feel dizzy.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel very tired and weak.
- Your mouth may feel dry and sore.
- This is normal after your treatment.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Eat foods that are safe for a neutropenic diet.
- Keep your blood sugar within your target range.
- Your goal this week is to rest and heal.
- Call your doctor if your temperature goes over 100.5°F.

**Week 2:**
- You might have a little more energy.
- Keep your activities light.
- Avoid crowds and people who are sick.
- Continue with your neutropenic diabetic diet.
- Monitor your blood sugar closely.
- Your goal is to walk a short distance daily.
- Call your doctor if you get a fever over 100.5°F.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel slightly stronger than last week.
- You can do more light chores if you feel up to it.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting.
- Follow your neutropenic diabetic eating plan.
- Watch for signs of infection.
- Your goal is to increase your walking time by 5 minutes.
- Call your doctor if your temperature is over 100.5°F.

**Week 4:**
- You should start to feel more consistent energy.
- Resume your usual activities as tolerated.
- Continue to lift no more than 10 pounds.
- Stick to your neutropenic diabetic diet.
- Keep your blood sugar levels stable.
- Your goal is to walk for 20 minutes daily.
- Call your doctor if you develop a fever over 100.5°F.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Recovery takes time after high-dose treatment.
- You should notice steady improvement over weeks.
- Keep following your dietary and activity guidelines.
- Contact your doctor with any concerns.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Breathing trouble or fast: Your body needs oxygen fast.
- Chest pain or pressure: Your heart needs help now.
- Signs of stroke: face droops, arm is weak, trouble speaking.
- Uncontrolled bleeding: Blood loss must stop right now.
- Loss of consciousness: You cannot wake up or respond.
- Seizure: Your brain is not working right now.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 100.5: You may have an infection.
- Confusion or acting strange: Your brain is not working right.
- Trouble breathing: You may not get enough oxygen.
- Not able to keep fluids down: You need hydration now.
- Pain gets worse: Your pain medicine is not enough.
- Falling down: You may have been hurt badly.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Questions about medicine: Your nurse can help you plan.
- Rash not getting better: A rash needs careful watching.
- Feeling tired: You may need rest and slow down.
